function: Joint transmit, reflection and receive beamforming for double-active-RIS ISAC, maximizing the sum of minimum sensing SINRs under communication rate constraints (p. 3).
system: Nt=10-antenna ISAC BS, K=2 single-antenna users, J=3 targets, two active RISs with M=25 elements each, no direct BS-user link; frequency band not stated (pp. 3, 9).
method: Deep reinforcement learning: TD3 actor-critic with feedforward networks, and GAN-TD3 where a generator-discriminator pair replaces the critic; trained online by agent-environment interaction (pp. 6-8).
data_channel: Custom simulator: Rician user-RIS1 links (kappa=10), LoS elsewhere, path-loss exponent 2.2; no dataset, agent trains and tests in the same simulated environment (pp. 4, 9).
test_conditions: One simulated setup; sweeps over M and Nt are convergence curves per value, P sweep averaged over 30 episodes; no unseen scenario tested (pp. 9-11).
baselines: Learned: TD3 variant, DDPG benchmark, and GAN-TD3 on a passive RIS; no non-learned method (optimization, random or fixed RIS) is compared (pp. 10-11).
metrics: Smoothed episode reward, episode sensing SINR (sum over L slots of the minimum sensing SINR), average episode reward versus power, and GPU training time (pp. 10-11).
complexity: Order of training complexity given for TD3 (Eq. 30, p. 7) and GAN-TD3 (Eq. 38, p. 8); GPU training time versus M in Fig. 8 (p. 10).
q1_support: p. 4: "Assume that the channels between the active RIS 1 and users are Rician channels [27]." The other links are LoS steering-vector models (p. 4); no 3GPP model, DeepMIMO or measured data is mentioned.
q2_support: p. 10: "each algorithm converges to a higher episode sensing SINR with M" shows convergence curves per configuration (M, Nt); no test in an unseen scenario, band, dataset or configuration after training is reported.
q3_support: p. 10: "we consider the deep deterministic policy gradient (DDPG) algorithm as a benchmark"; p. 11: passive RIS benchmark "the GAN-TD3 is utilized". Learned baseline present, but no non-learned method (optimization, random or fixed RIS) is compared; Table I (p. 2) is qualitative.
q4_support: p. 8: "The computational complexity of GAN-TD3-based algorithm can be formulated as" the order in Eq. (38); p. 10: "Fig. 8 shows the GPU training time versus M".
q5_support: p. 9: "If not specified, we set Nt = 10, L = 20, M = 25" defines the paper's own simulated environment; no code or data link, no public dataset, and no measured data is mentioned.
notes: ISAC beamforming with two active RISs learned by TD3 and GAN-TD3, so area 5 (ISAC wins over area 3). Table I and Table II were read from page images (pp. 2, 9). TD3 and the passive-RIS GAN-TD3 are variants of the proposed method and do not count as baselines. The abstract claims better generalization (p. 1) but no unseen condition is tested.
